items.title: Taiwan elections: Candidate criticised by China concedes Taipei mayoral race
paras: Puma Shen and Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te appear on stage. ( Reuters: Ann Wang )
Taiwan's ruling party candidate has conceded defeat in the Taipei mayoral election after local elections across the island's 22 cities and counties.
Democratic Progressive Party candidate Puma Shen's campaign had crumbled under pressure from China.
The nine-in-one elections saw voters cast ballots for local leaders and a referendum on nuclear energy.
Taiwan's ruling party candidate has conceded defeat in the Taipei mayoral election as results emerged from local elections across the island's 22 cities and counties.
Democratic Progressive Party candidate Puma Shen mounted a strong challenge to incumbent Mayor Chiang Wan-an but fell short of returning the city to DPP control for the first time since 1994.
"I know there's many people crying here. I want to thank every person who voted for me," Mr Shen told thousands of supporters after conceding.
Mr Shen, whom Beijing has labelled a separatist, said he had called Mr Chiang to congratulate him.
With votes from 1,606 of 1,790 polling stations counted — or almost 90 per cent — Mr Chiang had about 53.8 per cent of the vote to Mr Shen's 45.6 per cent, according to the electoral authorities.
The capital has traditionally been a stronghold of the opposition Nationalist Party, also known as the Kuomintang or KMT, which favours closer ties with China.
Traditionally, the KMT has performed well in local elections. In 2022, the DPP won in only five of 22 localities.
Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te campaigned for DPP candidates, appearing on Thursday night to support his party's mayoral candidate in Taoyuan City.
DPP candidate Puma Shen on stage after losing his bid to win the Taipei mayorship in Taipei. ( Reuters: Ann Wang )

Unlike presidential elections — when relations with China and Beijing's pressure on the self-ruled island are major issues — Saturday's vote focused more on local concerns, including social welfare benefits and other livelihood issues.
Initially viewed as a long shot, Mr Shen was known for his work organising civil defence courses.
He gained attention and support while campaigning on issues such as planting more trees and making city government more responsive.
His campaign unfolded under pressure from Beijing, which imposed sanctions on him and launched an investigation into his activities.
The Chinese government claims Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out force to annex it.
Taiwanese authorities have accused Beijing of attempting to sow distrust in the island's electoral system, allegations that Chinese authorities have rejected.
Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported about 33 sorties by Chinese warplanes, including bombers and fighter jets, toward the island between Friday and Saturday.
Chiang Wan-an (centre), of the opposition party KMT, at his campaign headquarters. ( Reuters: Yu Chih Wei )
As well as electing local leaders, voters also cast their ballots in a referendum to overturn a policy that banned nuclear power.
Supporters say additional energy sources are needed to meet the artificial intelligence industry's growing demand for electricity.
Voter Chang Li-fen said the economy was her foremost concern, but declined to say whom she had voted for.
"In France and in Italy, people are protesting because of energy costs, which raised the cost of living, so I think the economy is most important."
Mr Shen travelled in a motorcade across the city, stopping for 15 minutes at a time to greet the crowds of supporters.
Chiang held a Friday night rally with other KMT city council members, with supporters waving balloons, flags and light-up sticks to cheer him on.

items.title: One Nation finds its base in regional Victoria
paras: One Nation lead candidate for Western Victoria Chris Burson believes in the rise of One Nation ( ABC News: Harrison Tippet )
Shortly before the election polls closed on Saturday, Chris Burson was standing with a trio of his fellow One Nation candidates outside a Geelong polling booth.
The team was excited to see just how well they would do in the count, particularly following pre-election polling predicting the rise of One Nation.
They were equal parts confident and circumspect. A primary vote explosion seemed likely, but so too did difficult preference flows.
One Nation enjoyed a surge in voter support in regional Victoria on election day. ( ABC News: Jeremy Story Carter )
"I think there's a real vibe that things are going to change in not just Victoria, but Geelong," Mr Burson, the party's lead candidate for Western Victoria, said.
As one of the slowest, and most complicated election night counts neared midnight on Saturday, it would appear Mr Burson was right.
One Nation had asserted itself as the most disruptive force ever seen in a Victorian election, largely driven by its rise in the regions.

Numbers will fluctuate as vote counting continues on Sunday and into the next week, but the proportion of One Nation voters in regional Victoria compared to Melbourne early in the count is extremely telling.
One Nation has found its heartland in regional Victoria. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
A snapshot of the count at 9:15pm on Saturday had One Nation holding 15.7 per cent of the total primary vote count in metropolitan Victoria, compared to 32.3 per cent of the vote in the regions.
The question now will be how that vote translates to lower or upper house seats in the regions.
On Saturday evening, One Nation's Eureka candidate Paul Ballinger said he was not getting ahead of himself, despite a strong start in the polls.
He said the rise of One Nation was simple: voters were sick of "professional politicians".
"They've never actually been out in the real world," Mr Ballinger said.
Despite the huge primary vote trickling in throughout Saturday evening, the orange wave faced complicated preference flows which could dampen the surge in votes.
Prior to election day, Narracan, Morwell and Murray Plains were all seen as seats One Nation had a strong chance of taking.
Member for Narracan Wayne Farnham looks like he may hold off a One Nation surge ( ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery )
But — with more counting to come — taking more than 40 per cent of primary votes in all three seats as of 11pm on Saturday had not translated to wins for One Nation.
Counting and preferences made the seats near impossible to call on Saturday night, but all three looked on track to be won by the Coalition.
As vote counting closed on Saturday evening, the Coalition seemed poised to convert a strong primary and favourable preferences to winning seats across the regions.
As her own seat hung in the balance on Saturday evening, Labor Wendouree MP Juliana Addison said it had been an "extraordinary day for democracy".
"We have seen the emergence of One Nation, we've seen a huge Greens vote — this has really shaken everything up," Ms Addison said.
She also voiced her disappointment that Premier Ben Carroll lost his seat of Niddrie, in what was a catastrophic election for Labor.
"I'm sad for Ben. He's given so much to the Labor Party, but I'll have to process that," she said.

While a slow and complicated vote count continues to play out in coming days, One Nation is already looking toward the more favourable expected preference flows of the upper house, where they hope to see votes translate to One Nation MPs.
Ben Carroll conceded defeat at the Victorian state election, also losing his seat. ( ABC News: James Oaten )
"We're more likely to have success in the upper house than the lower house, as we've talked about before, because of those preferences," Pauline Hanson's chief of staff Chris Taylor said.
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson addressed an adoring crowd on Saturday evening, announcing the party's mission to disrupt Victoria's political status quo was already a success.
"One Nation is snapping at the heels of the political establishment, Labor and Liberal both, and they know it," she said.

items.title: Labor MPs are in 'disbelief' after electoral annihilation in Victoria
paras: Ben Carroll used his concession speech to highlight Labor achievements during 12 years in government. ( AAP: Con Chronis )
Tonight's results represent electoral annihilation of the party in Victoria.
"We [Labor] need a fresh start," said another MP, who should narrowly hold on, in an apparent nod to Liberal leader Jess Wilson's commanding campaign .
Not long ago, Labor seemed to be the natural owners of the state's politics.
Tonight Labor candidates and senior party figures barely had the words to explain how they had fallen from the 56-seat highs they experienced only last election under Daniel Andrews.
Labor's longstanding so-called red wall in the north and west of Melbourne didn't just lose a brick, it took out the premier.
Sydenham will fall. Sunbury. Point Cook. Possibly Greenvale, Kalkallo, Werribee, St Albans, Tarneit, Essendon.
In a gracious concession speech, Carroll listed off Labor achievements during 12 years in government — and there are many.
He spruiked Labor policies he was proud of from major infrastructure projects such as the Metro Tunnel and level crossing removals to free TAFE, teacher pay deals and voluntary assisted dying.
He pointed to Labor's decade of work to deliver of a Treaty with Victoria's First Peoples.
For the first time since taking the leadership, Carroll seemed to say Daniel Andrews' and Jacinta Allan's names with ease on Saturday night.
Who becomes the next Victorian Labor leader, responsible for rebuilding, will depend on who is left. ( AAP: Con Chronis )
For some in Labor, the campaign was so conscious of avoiding its ghosts — like corruption on its transformative infrastructure projects — that it erased its victories from the narrative entirely.
Deputy leader Gabrielle Williams said Labor failed to learn from hits to its primary vote in its heartland in 2022 and at last year's Werribee byelection.
"There were many inflection points that should have given us cause to listen or, more importantly, to respond."
Deputy Labor leader Gabrielle Williams on election night. ( ABC News: Alonso Gajardo )
Outgoing MP Gary Maas, who leaves the parliament after deciding not to recontest in Narre Warren South, told the ABC that Labor forgot who it represented.
"Labor's primary rightfully bottomed," said Maas, who has Sri Lankan heritage.
"We traditionally rely on our multicultural and multi-faith communities yet our multicultural and multi-faith communities aren't reflected as actual MPs in Labor governments.
"Standing in the middle trying to straddle things meant standing for nothing," she wrote on social media.
The party had been "trading values to quell front pages instead of holding the line", Terpstra said.
"We need to assess why working class people abandoned us in this election and work hard to win them back," Sydenham candidate Uroš Rasic told the ABC.
"Labor needs to take a good look at itself and rebuild trust with Victorians."
In the eastern suburbs, Labor won't make the two-party preferred result in seats the party held a day ago.
Not that this was ever Labor territory, but the party bet big under Daniel Andrews.
Once the final preferences are distributed, Victoria's 61st parliament will likely include just 15 Labor MPs in an 88 seat house.
Who becomes the next Victorian Labor leader, responsible for rebuilding, will depend on who is left.

items.title: RBI Issues Amendment Directions on ‘Suspected Money Mule Accounts to Prevent Cyber-enabled Financial Frauds’
paras: The Reserve Bank had issued the draft Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 on September 11, 2026, for seeking feedback from stakeholders. The draft Amendment Directions proposed a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) laying down a uniform, time-bound procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected to be linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds, and to remove such holds in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), while protecting genuine customers from inconvenience. 2. Feedback received on the above draft Directions has been examined and the consequent modifications have been suitably incorporated in the final Amendment Directions. A statement on the feedback received is provided in the Annex . Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following Amendment Directions, which shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or from such earlier date as a bank may decide to implement the SOP. Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Know Your Customer) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Know Your Customer) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Know Your Customer) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks - Know Your Customer) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Know Your Customer) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1584

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

🇮🇳 sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA. The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products,… pic.twitter.com/ZlFiKOfezx

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
paras: buttons are back, kind of 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price Kindles are getting costlier faster than they’re getting better.

21 ... ... ... Credit: Andrew Cunningham Credit: Andrew Cunningham Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven’t been immune. That’s why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years ago . “New thing, better features, same price” used to be a reliable formula, but now you’re lucky if you can get the same thing for barely more than before.

The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year’s $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you’re choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models.

The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic.

It’s an exceptionally nice reader, and if you’re down with paying even more for it, longtime page-turn button holdouts can recover their precious buttons while still getting the benefits of new, fast Kindle hardware. With the exception of one regression—wireless charging, a feature of the 2024 Signature Edition that has been removed here—it’s the fastest and nicest Kindle you can get. It’s mostly the value, or lack thereof, that leaves a bad taste in one’s mouth.

Andrew Cunningham Unlike the 2021 or 2024 Kindle Paperwhite updates, the 2026 Paperwhite doesn’t include any notable screen or lighting upgrades. Anyone upgrading from a two- or three-generation-old version of the hardware will still get an upgrade, but the 2026 Paperwhite isn’t doing a ton to push the category forward. And while speed increases were front-and-center in Amazon’s promotional material for the 2024 Paperwhite, Amazon isn’t highlighting any particular gains for this year’s Paperwhite (the base Kindle does apparently open books 30 percent faster than the previous-generation Kindle, though).

But the Paperwhite and this year’s basic Kindle both make a couple of tweaks worth mentioning that don’t really show up on a spec sheet. One is that the device’s power button moves from the bottom edge to the top-right edge, a small change I appreciate because I’ve accidentally pressed the bottom-mounted power button all the times I’ve tried to set the Kindle on the edge of something. The other is that the devices now have user-replaceable batteries, a change made in part to comply with right-to-repair regulations going into effect in some countries.

Whether you’re buying the standard plastic-backed Paperwhite or the aluminum Signature Edition, you’re still getting a 7-inch 300 PPI screen with a front light that can adjust its color temperature as well as its brightness, which I find makes the Paperwhite easier on the eyes than the harsher, more bluish-tinted front light on older Kindles and the basic 2026 Kindle. The plastic Paperwhite is a smidge lighter than the 2024 version, and the Signature Edition is a little heavier (thanks in part to the aluminum casing), though not by a lot in either direction.

Whether it’s faster than the 2024 Paperwhite or not, the snappy and fluid performance I observed while using that device is definitely present in this one. The E-Ink screen still puts a cap on exactly how fluid and responsive the device can feel, but you rarely feel the big gap between your touch input and the device responding to that input like you can on most older Kindles. (I tried repeatedly to run the old Google Octane 2.0 benchmark I used to get a sense of the 2024 Paperwhite’s relative performance, but it could never complete a run in either the 2026 Kindle or the 2026 Paperwhite’s browser, for whatever reason).

The 2026 Kindle (right) and the 2018-era Paperwhite. Same size screen, much smaller device. Andrew Cunningham The 2026 Kindle is cute, but it’s more expensive than the Paperwhite was a few years ago. Andrew Cunningham The 2026 Kindle is cute, but it’s more expensive than the Paperwhite was a few years ago. Andrew Cunningham The Kindle has a hard plastic back, but there’s an aluminum version too. Andrew Cunningham The Kindle has a hard plastic back, but there’s an aluminum version too. Andrew Cunningham The 2026 Kindle is cute, but it’s more expensive than the Paperwhite was a few years ago. Andrew Cunningham The Kindle has a hard plastic back, but there’s an aluminum version too. Andrew Cunningham I didn’t spend as much time with it, but I did test the basic 6-inch Kindle alongside the Paperwhite Signature Edition.

Overall, I like the updated look and feel of the redesigned Kindle, particularly the fact that the screen and bezel are now flush, as the last few Paperwhites have been. And despite using the same 6-inch screen size as older Paperwhites, Amazon has significantly shrunk the overall size and weight of the device. It doesn’t quite look like a “Kindle mini” next to the current Paperwhite, but it’s not far off.

But you’re still getting less for your money than you were a few years ago. If you compare the 2026 Kindle to the 2024 or 2022 model, and you ignore what each one of those devices cost to buy, it looks like slow and steady improvement. But the fact is that you can pay $150 for this Kindle and lose important features, like the warm light and waterproofing, that Amazon offered in the 2021 Paperwhite for just $140 back in 2021.
That’s just the reality of buying technology right now. “Get more for the same money” is out. Now if you want more, you have to pay more.
The new Paperwhite Signature Edition’s biggest upgrade, should you choose to pay for it, is the addition of page-turn buttons. Page-turn buttons by proxy, at least.

The Signature Edition adds iPad-style copper contacts on the back, and for another $80 (on top of the $250 you’ll pay for the Kindle) you can buy a Kindle Page Turn Cover in various colors that connects to those contacts with pogo pins. It’s the cover that adds the buttons. Amazon also offers a $60 charging stand that uses the pins, the closest equivalent for the now-removed wireless charging feature.

The cover really does make the new Paperwhite look and feel a bit more like a Frankenstein Kindle Oasis, right down to the asymmetrical edge that the button area adds. And the page-turn buttons themselves feel good and work well. The physical feedback from clicky buttons and the Kindle’s overall responsiveness both make page turns feel nearly instantaneous when you press it to turn a single page. Clicking the buttons quickly to turn multiple pages still gets bogged down a little.

Functionally, the worst things I can say about the Page Turn Cover are that it adds to the reader’s size and weight, and the power button doesn’t feel nearly as good as the page-turn buttons. The case’s “button” is basically a little plastic nub that pushes in the device’s actual built-in power button. At least with the hardware I bought, the case’s button feels like it can’t consistently reach the device button, which means it wasn’t always reliable. This is partly moot because opening and closing the cover also wakes and sleeps the device.

Amazon offers one cheaper option for every other Kindle that can run the newest version of the Kindle operating system: a $35 remote control-style Kindle Click . As a completely separate accessory you have to hold or rest on something in order to use, I don’t find this to be a particularly compelling solution to the “no buttons” problem. But it’s also the only version of “clickable buttons” that Amazon offers for less than $330. It is what it is.

The Kindle Click requires a Kindle running version 5.20.1.0.2 or later of the Kindle operating system. Currently, that version only runs on the 2024 and 2026 Kindles, plus 2022’s Kindle Scribe. It seems as though Amazon has gotten stingier with long-tail Kindle OS updates than it was in 2024, when all Kindles going back to 2018 could run the same software. The 2018 Kindles currently top out at 5.18, while the other 2021/22 Kindles stop at 5.19.

The last reader Amazon offered with page-turn buttons was 2019’s $249 Kindle Oasis, which was dinged pretty much across the board for being “expensive.” Today’s Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition will cost you just as much, but charge you $80 extra for the case and buttons. It’s a nicer reader in some important ways, most notably its USB-C port and much-improved performance. But that’s still a pretty substantial increase for anyone with an aging Oasis they’d like to replace with a Paperwhite-plus-case.

That’s my response to the new Paperwhite and to all of this year’s Kindle releases in a nutshell. They are nice, but they’re so much more expensive than Kindles have been in the very recent past that it’s hard to feel very enthusiastic about them. The basic Kindle-versus-old-Paperwhite comparison is the one that’s the most frustrating—the Kindle has picked up Paperwhite-style pricing more quickly than it has added Paperwhite features.

Hopefully we’ll see third-party accessory makers figure out support for their own pogo-pinned accessories, to bring the pricing down just a little bit. Otherwise, if you don’t need or want buttons, the best way to find a good deal on a Kindle is probably to buy an old one—the 2024 Paperwhite is $130 right now , and you might want to get it while the getting’s good.

items.title: Dan Evans makes comment about his controversial retirement earlier this year after playing exhibition in Russia
paras: Dan Evans only retired earlier this year, but has already begun trying his hand at exhibition matches. However, few could possibly have predicted that his first would be so surprising or controversial.

Just yesterday, the Brit faced current WTA Tour star Diana Shnaider in a timed match in St Petersburg, Russia, losing 5-2. Afterwards, Evans spoke about his mini Battle of the Sexes , which seemingly nobody saw coming.

Now, in another interview held at this most unusual of events, he has once again discussed his controversial retirement as well as his current plans to continue coaching a compatriot. In an interview shared by BB Tennis, he was asked about the decision to call time at Wimbledon earlier this year. It was one of the most talked-about moments in the lead-up to the third Grand Slam of the season, with the event criticised for not awarding Dan Evans a wildcard in his last ever tournament.

items.title: Victoria Mboko’s 2026 Season Recap: A Top-10 Breakthrough and a Promising Rise Interrupted by Injury
paras: Following her breakthrough campaign in 2025, when she won the Montreal WTA 1000 and Hong Kong titles, the Canadian teenager demonstrated that her arrival among the sport’s leading players was no coincidence. Three WTA finals, a fourth-round appearance at the Australian Open and a career-high ranking of #9 highlighted an impressive opening half of the campaign.

However, a knee injury sustained during the grass-court season disrupted her progress and prevented her from building on an encouraging start. The question for Mboko now will be how quickly she can regain her fitness and sharpness heading into 2027.

Mboko began the season strongly, reaching the final of the Adelaide International before losing to Mirra Andreeva 6-3 6-1. She subsequently reached the fourth round of the Australian Open , recording her best Grand Slam result to that point.

items.title: November 28, 1999: The day Pete Sampras won the ATP Finals for the fifth time
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to one of the most iconic moments in tennis history. On this day in 1999, Pete Sampras equaled Ivan Lendl’s record for the most season-ending ATP Finals titles won

On this day, November 28, 1999, Pete Sampras won the season-ending ATP Finals for the fifth time, tying Ivan Lendl’s record at the time. To achieve this feat, he defeated Andre Agassi in the final (6-1, 7-5, 6-4), although his long-time rival had outplayed him during the round-robin phase (6-2, 6-2).

For Sampras, it was a great way to finish a complicated year, during which he had to skip both the Australian Open and the US Open because of injuries and had lost his world No 1 spot. As for Agassi, who was enjoying the best season of his career, it was a reminder that his old rival would always be there to challenge him in the big events.

items.title: Alexandra Eala’s Remarkable Rise to the Top
paras: The 21-year-old transformed herself from one of the sport’s most promising prospects into an established name on the WTA Tour, collecting her first Tour-level singles title, achieving historic results at Grand Slams tournaments, and breaking into the world’s Top 15. Alexandra Eala entered 2026 looking to build on an impressive previous campaign.

After breaking into the WTA Top 100 in 2025, the challenge was to establish greater consistency and demonstrate that she could compete regularly against higher-ranked opponents. Eala showed signs of progress, reaching the semifinals of the ASB Classic in Auckland.

Although she experienced an early exit at the Australian Open , she quickly bounced back during the Middle Eastern swing. The Filipina reached the quarterfinals in both Abu Dhabi and Dubai, collecting valuable victories and gaining experience against established players.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
